Four years ago I had a #bronchoscopy. A trip to the Royal Brompton hospital in London confirmed I had Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (PPFE) is a rare lung disease, usually associated with scarring & #fibrosis of the lungs.The only treatment that would help would eventually be a lung transplant.My lung transplant journey began…. #hospital #lungdisease #lungtransplant #london #nhs

#Introducing myself 😊 I’m Sarah Jane, 33 years old and a grateful recipient of a single lung transplant this February 2022. I want to create a space where I can document my journey, both before and after transplant as it was a chapter of my life that I found both scary and rewarding in equal measure.So this is my journey. Starting in 2018 I went to the gp with shortness of breath, a dry cough and a chest x Ray showed significant scarring #pulmonaryfibrosis  #lungdisease #lungtransplant

These devices heat up various flavorings, nicotine, marijuana, or other potentially harmful substances. Nicotine is addictive, of course. COPD Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is the name for a group of lung conditions that cause breathing difficulties. It includes: emphysema – damage to the air sacs in the lungs chronic bronchitis – long-term inflammation of the airways COPD is a common condition that mainly affects middle-aged or older adults who smoke. Many people do not realise they have it. The breathing problems tend to get gradually worse over time and can limit your normal activities, although treatment can help keep the condition under control. Symptoms of COPD The main symptoms of COPD are: shortness of breath, particularly when you're active a persistent chesty cough with phlegm – some people may dismiss this as just a "smoker's cough" frequent chest infections persistent wheezing Without treatment, the symptoms usually get progressively worse. There may also be periods when they get suddenly worse, known as a flare-up or exacerbation. Find out more about the symptoms of COPD and Stop Smoking as soon as possoble. If your little (or big!) one has surgery scars, uses an insulin pump, needs a walker, wears a cranial therapy helmet or depends on a tablet and ear defenders (or any other aids), Nick and his team will make an exact replica in plushy form to keep them company along the way. How they manage to replicate any kind of medical aid/equipment is just brilliant.  This special plushy has NSIP, a rare type of pulmonary fibrosis, exactly like Boots. It’s been made for a couple of reasons - firstly, to make him smile 😀 and, secondly, as something the kids can mind if and when he goes in for a lung transplant operation. It’s already made all of us smile today 🥰 Please go and check out 3D Toyshop and donate if possible. Replacing Your Lungs With Someone Else’s #transplant Double lung transplants are among the most complex and risky surgical procedures, with a one-year survival rate of around 80% and a five-year survival rate of around 50%. The high risk associated with double lung transplants stems from several factors:  The complexity of the surgery: The procedure involves removing both of the recipient's diseased lungs and replacing them with two healthy donor lungs. This delicate and intricate operation requires highly skilled surgeons and a specialized team of medical professionals.  The risk of rejection: The recipient's immune system may recognize the transplanted lungs as foreign tissue and attack them, leading to organ rejection. This can be a life-threatening complication that requires ongoing immunosuppressive therapy.  The risk of infection: Immunosuppressive drugs, while necessary to prevent rejection, weaken the immune system, making the recipient more susceptible to infections. These infections can be serious and difficult to treat.  The risk of surgical complications: Like any major surgery, a double lung transplant carries the risk of complications such as bleeding, blood clots, pneumonia, and respiratory failure.  The long-term effects of immunosuppression: While immunosuppressive drugs are crucial for preventing rejection, long-term use can increase the risk of developing certain cancers, kidney disease, and other health problems.  doctors performing double lung transplant surgery Opens in a new window  www.massgeneral.org doctors performing double lung transplant surgery  Despite the risks, double lung transplants can offer a life-saving treatment option for people with end-stage lung disease. Careful patient selection, advanced surgical techniques, and improved immunosuppressive medications have contributed to improved survival rates in recent years. How Vaping Can Put You in Hospital #novape While vaping has been touted as a safer alternative to smoking traditional cigarettes, it is not without its risks. Inhaling the aerosol produced by e-cigarettes can expose your lungs to a variety of harmful substances, including: Nicotine: Nicotine is a highly addictive substance that can harm the developing brain in young people. It can also increase the risk of heart disease, stroke, and lung cancer. Flavorings: Some flavorings used in e-cigarettes have been linked to lung disease. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs): VOCs are harmful chemicals that can irritate the lungs and eyes. Heavy metals: Some e-cigarettes contain trace amounts of heavy metals, such as lead and nickel, which can be harmful to the nervous system.  In addition to these long-term health risks, vaping can also cause immediate side effects, such as: Coughing: Vaping can irritate the lining of the lungs and cause a cough. Shortness of breath: Vaping can make it difficult to breathe. Chest pain: Vaping can cause chest pain. Nausea and vomiting: Vaping can cause nausea and vomiting.  If you are considering vaping, it is important to be aware of the potential risks. Max was born with a left pulmonary artery sling, imperforate anus, tracheal stenosis, kidney reflux and a deformity of his left leg.  He had a stoma fitted when he was 1 day old and then had surgery to woden his trachea and reposition his left pulmonary artery at 5 months old. Max's recovery from this major surgery was tough and he had a cardiac arrest following it. He spent 10 weeks on a ventilator and had many failed extubations before he was able to step down to less invasive breathing support. He was also heavily sedated and the weaning process was really tough. He was finally discharged at 9 months old and is now able to have his bowel and limb surgeries. He is our hero.  #vacterl #vacterlawareness #limbdeformity #stomababy #trachealstenosis #breathingissues #cardiacarrest #hero #mumsoftiktok #momsoftiktok #fyp #medicalmom

"Shout out” to this kid, bless him. 4 years ago today vik had his first open heart surgery. He's been in and out of hospital since the age of 6 weeks old, been put to sleep more times than i can count and this will remain on going for the rest of his life. More open hearts, more coronary angiography procedures and it is not cureable. Every procedure form i sign says "to prolong life". We dont know what the future holds but it's all he's ever know. He remains procedure free for 2 years now, to allow his body to grow before another valve repair or replacement. Having a brother with Autism and in a single parent house hold this boy has had to grow up fast. So many people say hes an old soul. The nights i lay awake worrying about both there futures. Vik misses out a lot due to the high needs of his big brother but he hardly complains. He understands how lucky we are to have each other and my childrens challanges gives me more perspective on life and just how precious it is. Funny i called him Viktor before i knew what was coming. Adventure with disease ✌🏻 4am wake up calls for summer solstice. Took my anxious brain and painful body for a sunrise dip, coffee & silent disco. It’s the first time I’ve gone to @dawnstalkers solo. A daunting prospect but soothed by the fact I know  strangers at the seafront are generally very friendly.  My brain is overly anxious at the moment, I’ve been low in mood and my body has been a pain. I started cold water dipping in Dec 2020. my first time was  done as a ‘joke’, a laugh.  I’ve been hooked ever since but have missed out for a while. I find the chilly water soothing for my soul & my misbehaving body. It is very much not a joke, with bad lungs I really have to focus on my breathing. I never regret it.  I had a swim, a coffee and a little boogie solo but surrounded by smiling faces. There is something incredibly joyful about seeing humans living their best lives. The dance performances I witnessed by some very main character energy women soothed my soul and my brain.  After a little boogie, it was time to sit and listen to the waves for a few quiet moments, away from the crowd before I jumped back in Lara the Landy to return home to my dogs. Who greeted me like I’d been gone several days and not a couple of hours whilst they dozed.  Life can be physically & mentally painful but there is also joy to be had. A primary school teacher of mine once told me, it’s still okay to find moments to smile even when you don’t feel well X  #lungdisease #hypersensitivitypneumonitis #ILD #interstitiallungdisease #pulmonaryfibrosis #lunghealth #livingwithdisease

The pulse oximeter is very, very important. If you have breathing problems. Maybe asthma or any other breathing problems, to be honest. You need to get yourself one. It's quite durable. It's small. It's sold in the pharmacies. You don't need to see your doctor, It reads your heart rate per minute. And it also gives you your oxygen saturation level. That is what alerts you to know if you are in crisis and need to call for help,  That will tell you what number a perfect saturation level is 100 for a "healthy person" mine normally sits at 97/98, but can go down to 94, which is not good, so this helps me monitor it myself and to try and get myself back up, and if all fails I call 111.  If you do anything today please go get yourself one. #kikisnuggets #sarcoidosiswarrior #chronicillness #breathing #oximeter #pulseoximeter #lungdisease
